title: Cytochrome c: structure and role
question: and what about cytochrome c?
canonical_question: What does cytochrome c do in the electron transport chain?
summary: Cytochrome c is a small mobile electron carrier.
It shuttles electrons from Complex III to Complex IV.

reuse.rationale: No existing node describes the mobile carrier between complexes.

sections.heading: A small mobile carrier
sections.body_md: Cytochrome c is a small protein that carries electrons. Unlike the large complexes fixed in the membrane, it is loosely attached to the membrane surface and can move along it. That mobility lets it act as a shuttle.

sections.heading: What it connects
sections.body_md: Cytochrome c picks up an electron from Complex III and drops it off at Complex IV. By ferrying electrons between these two fixed stations, it keeps the chain flowing without either complex having to touch the other.

key_points: Cytochrome c is a small, mobile electron carrier.
It shuttles electrons from Complex III to Complex IV.
core.bridge_to_parent: It fills in one of the upstream carriers named among the essential proteins.
